title: OrionAI - POC scoping: workload modeling & benchmarks
meeting_summary: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for OrionAI's customer-facing assistant. Discussed QPS/concurrency targets, input/output token distributions, latency SLOs, security requirements (VPC, KMS, SOC2), benchmark plan, and 4-week pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: customer to share sample logs and prompts, Redwood to propose POC plan + pricing and schedule benchmark run.

transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sam Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam Zhao (Redwood Solutions), Markus Lee (OrionAI Head of ML), Jenna Park (Infra Lead), Raul Gomez (CTO), Sofia Ruiz (PM)

Summary:
- Quick intro and goals: scope POC, define success criteria, size workload and plan benchmarks.
- Focus areas: QPS and concurrency targets, input/output token distribution, latency/cost SLOs, security constraints, timeline.

Topics:
1) Current production profile and constraints
2) Success criteria for POC
3) Traffic modeling: QPS, concurrency, token distribution
4) Benchmark plan and timeline
5) Security and deployment model (hosted vs dedicated, VPC)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sam Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round robin, hi I'm Sam, AE at Redwood, I'll coordinate the POC.
[00:12] Markus Lee: Markus here — head of ML at OrionAI. we're building the public assistant for our finance product. main ask today is to size a POC and decide if we go hosted or dedicated.
[00:25] Priya Singh: Hey all, Priya SE. I'll run the benchmarking and help with model selection and perf tuning.
[00:32] Jenna Park: Jenna, infra lead. i'll be handling networking, security checks.
[00:37] Raul Gomez: Raul, CTO - interested in cost and ops implications.
[00:42] Sofia Ruiz: Sofia, product. interested in success metrics.
[00:46] Sam Carter: Great. quick context — Markus, can you describe current traffic? average QPS, peak bursts, typical prompt/response sizes?
[00:55] Markus Lee: Sure. today in alpha we see roughly 10 QPS average, peaks up to ~120 QPS during marketing spikes. concurrency around 8-12 on average; during spikes we hit 40-80 concurrent in a few minutes window. Most user prompts are short — 20 to 80 tokens — but we also have longer context queries, maybe up to 300 tokens occasionally. Responses currently average 180 tokens, 90th pct around 420. token distribution is pretty skewed — 60% short, 30% medium, 10% long.
[02:03] Priya Singh: that's helpful. and are you doing multi-turn chat with KV cache or stateless calls?
[02:09] Markus Lee: both. majority stateless, but the assistant retains short-term context for some flows. KV cache usage would help for multi-turn.
[02:16] Priya Singh: ok. so for modeling we should treat two traffic classes: stateless single-call flows and multi-turn with KV cache warmed. We'll simulate both.
[02:24] Sam Carter: What's your target latency SLO? p95, p99?
[02:28] Sofia Ruiz: product wants p95 < 800ms for short prompts, ideally < 500ms. p99 we accept up to 2s for long generation.
[02:38] Raul Gomez: cost is also important — we're looking at rough cost per 1k tokens to compare hosted vs dedicated.
[02:45] Sam Carter: Good. Redwood can provide both hosted and dedicated estimates. For POC we'll benchmark on equivalent model variants and give per-token cost, plus latency percentiles.
[02:55] Priya Singh: For traffic sizing: for the POC we usually model a baseline of 1x production (your average), 3x for realistic stress, and a 10x burst for resilience. so if you have 10 QPS average, we'll run tests at 10, 30, and 100 QPS with realistic concurrency patterns. does that align?
[03:14] Markus Lee: yes that sounds right — 100 QPS burst is representative of our worst marketing event.
[03:19] Jenna Park: network — if we do dedicated, we'll need peering and a private subnet; security team also wants KMS integration and audit logs. SOC2 is mandatory.
[03:29] Sam Carter: Redwood Private supports VPC and customer-managed KMS, plus audit logs. We'll include that in the security appendix.
[03:36] Priya Singh: on model sizes — what generation quality do you need? Are you okay with an open LLM equivalent to 13B, or do you need 70B-class?
[03:44] Markus Lee: currently quality at 13B-ish is fine for most flows, but for financial summarization and compliance messages we lean on a stronger 33B/70B model. For POC we want to validate 13B for latency/cost and run one 33B run for quality check.
[03:59] Sam Carter: Makes sense: baseline 13B family for SLOs and costs, one run on 33B for qualitative checks.
[04:06] Priya Singh: token-level distribution is key for batching and KV cache behavior. from Markus' numbers: median input 45 tokens, median output 180 tokens. we'll prepare distributions: inputs: 20% < 30 tokens, 60% 30-100, 20% >100; outputs: 50% 0-150, 35% 150-400, 15% 400+. Does that match your observed logs?
[04:34] Markus Lee: yes that's a good approximation. I'll share a histogram.
[04:39] Priya Singh: for concurrency modeling, we'll simulate 95th percentile inter-arrival bursts: short bursts of 90-100 QPS sustained for 2-5 minutes, to evaluate autoscaling and cold-start behaviors.
[04:52] Raul Gomez: what about batching? we prefer lower latency, but if batching gives 2-3x cost reduction at small latency increase maybe it's worth it.
[05:01] Priya Singh: we'll test batching windows: 1) no batching (single-request), 2) micro-batching (10-30ms), 3) larger batching (50-200ms). We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. Redwood Optimize will recommend settings per workload.
[05:17] Sam Carter: Security/Compliance quick check — Jenna, besides SOC2 and KMS, any region/data residency constraints?
[05:23] Jenna Park: EU customer data must stay in eu-west; we have customers in EU, so for the POC we'd like to run at least one benchmark in the eu region.
[05:31] Sam Carter: Redwood can route traffic to region and we can provision a eu-dedicated pilot if needed. We'll note that as a requirement.
[05:37] Sofia Ruiz: success criteria for POC — product wants: 1) p95 latency < 800ms for short prompts on baseline model, 2) cost per 1k tokens less than X (we'll define X after Redwood pricing), 3) observed quality parity with current baseline on 33B check, 4) seamless VPC connectivity and KMS integration.
[05:58] Sam Carter: we'll produce a success checklist with measurable thresholds.
[06:03] Priya Singh: benchmark plan (high level): week 0: get logs and prompt set; week 1: synthetic traffic runs (10/30/100 QPS) on 13B hosted; week 2: dedicated baseline run and tuning (batching/quantization); week 3: 33B quality run and end-to-end validation; week 4: results, recommendations, cost model, and next steps for production. Does 4 weeks work?
[06:27] Markus Lee: yes that's our expectation. We might want faster turnaround on weeks 1-2 if we can.
[06:31] Sam Carter: we'll try to compress the schedule if logs arrive this week.
[06:35] Jenna Park: on benchmarks, we need an SLA on test environment stability — e.g. isolated capacity so your test doesn't get noisy neighbors. For dedicated you'll get reserved pools; for hosted we'll request a quiet window but want to accept some variance.
[06:50] Priya Singh: for hosted tests we try to use pinned instances / reserved capacity for test windows to reduce variability. we'll annotate noise in results.
[06:58] Raul Gomez: are there standard benchmark artifacts you provide?
[07:02] Priya Singh: yes — latency histograms, token throughput, cost projection, CPU/GPU utilization logs, batch size distributions, KV cache hit rates. we'll share a benchmark dashboard link after runs.
[07:13] Sam Carter: risks: model mismatch on quality, network egress costs, and under-estimated burst sizing — we'll surface mitigation and fallback (auto-failover to smaller model) in the POC plan.
[07:26] Sofia Ruiz: can Redwood run replay of real user traffic? that's important for multi-turn behavior.
[07:32] Priya Singh: yes, with anonymized logs we can run replay tests, including multi-turn sequences and KV cache warmup patterns. Please ensure personally identifiable info is removed.
[07:43] Markus Lee: we'll anonymize. we'll include prompt IDs and timestamps.
[07:48] Sam Carter: one more thing — do you have a preferred success metric for cost? absolute dollars or relative improvement vs current infra?
[07:56] Raul Gomez: relative improvement would help, but we also need absolute monthly cost at expected peak. so both.
[08:03] Priya Singh: Got it. We'll produce cost per 1k input+output tokens and a monthly cost projection at average and 3x loads.
[08:13] Sam Carter: Ok let's capture next steps and owners — we'll send a draft POC scope and pricing, Priya will prep benchmark harness, Markus to share logs and prompt sets, Jenna to share networking constraints and SOC2 contacts.
[08:25] Sofia Ruiz: timeline constraints — legal needs 2 weeks to review an MSA, so we need to plan contracting after results.
[08:33] Sam Carter: noted. we'll try to keep POC results ready before contract review window.
[08:38] Priya Singh: any other questions?
[08:40] Jenna Park: question about encryption at rest for KV cache — is it customer-managed?
[08:45] Sam Carter: Yes, with Private we support customer KMS/HSM. Redwood-hosted can also integrate with customer KMS for key wrapping. We'll add details in the security doc.
[08:56] Markus Lee: OK, sounds good. we'll send logs by Tuesday.
[08:59] Sam Carter: Great. we'll follow up with POC scope and schedule. Thanks everyone.
[09:05] Meeting end.

Notes on modeling details (auto-generated):
- Traffic classes: 1) Stateless single-turn: 60% of calls, median 45 input tokens, median 120 output tokens. 2) Multi-turn with KV cache: 40% calls, longer session lengths and higher output tokens.
- Planned test QPS: baseline 10 QPS, stress 30 QPS, burst 100 QPS.
- Concurrency goals: average concurrency ~12, target p95 concurrency handling up to 80-100 for short bursts.
- Token distributions: inputs median 45, outputs median 180; P90 output ~420.
- Latency targets: p95 < 800ms (short prompts), p99 < 2s (long).
- Benchmark matrix: 13B hosted (no batching, micro-batching, larger batching), 13B dedicated, 33B quality run (single requests), KV cache warm vs cold tests.
- Deliverables: benchmark report (latency histograms, throughput, cost projections), config recommendations (batching/quantization), final POC success checklist.

References shared in call:
- Internal Redwood POC template (link: redwood.com/poc-template)
- Benchmark dashboard (to be shared after runs)
- Security appendix (will attach SOC2 report and KMS integration guide)

End of transcript.
